discussion_comments.comment_body: AI Review: When an editor group is maximized, sibling groups remain in `mainPart.groups` with their `activeEditor` populated even though GridView hides them. This mapping therefore keeps counting hidden siblings in `visibleEditorCount` and `visibleChatEditorCount` (for example, two active Chat Editors still report 2 when only one is displayed). Maximizing/restoring also emits `onDidChangeGroupMaximized`, which this contribution does not subscribe to, so no corrected snapshot is logged. Please subscribe to that event and compute visible counts from only displayed groups while retaining all groups for open/group totals; add a maximization regression test.

Addressed in 8275eeab4c3. Open/group totals still use all main-part groups, while visible counts now exclude hidden siblings when `mainPart.hasMaximizedGroup()` is true. The contribution subscribes to `onDidChangeGroupMaximized`, and the telemetry test covers two open Chat Editors with only the maximized group counted as visible.

AI Review: Nit: Could we add focused browser coverage for both new focus-suppression paths? `compositionend` should update search without the next-button/input focus bounce, while a `hasFindResult` callback after a new `compositionstart` should also leave focus untouched. A deterministic `WebviewFindWidget` test can use a mock delegate, count focus/blur events, and retain a normal-input control assertion. There is currently no automated coverage for either path.

Added focused browser coverage in 554413076ac:

- `compositionend` updates search without the next-button/input focus bounce.
- `hasFindResult` arriving after a new `compositionstart` leaves focus unchanged.
- Normal input still updates search and restores focus.

The tests use a mock delegate and record actual DOM focus/blur events. All three pass in Chromium and WebKit.

I also verified that removing each focus-suppression guard independently causes its corresponding regression test to fail.
@wibaek The tests are failing it seems...

Addressed in 0ae6fdbe9d9 — the hand-rolled `HydrationTestFileService` is gone. The hydration suite now builds a real `FileService` backed by `InMemoryFileSystemProvider` (same setup as `workspacePluginSettingsService.test.ts`), seeds `installed.json` and the marketplace manifest via `fileService.writeFile`, and drops the `as unknown as IFileService` cast entirely. If `FileBackedInstalledPluginsStore` starts calling additional `IFileService` APIs, these tests will exercise them through the real surface.

🤖 **[P1] This More button cannot be activated from the keyboard.** It remains a native tab stop, but Enter/Space bubbles to `_onTreeKeyDown`, which resolves the parent row, clicks the enablement toggle, and calls `preventDefault()`. That suppresses the button's native click, so keyboard users toggle the tool set instead of opening this menu. The former row context-menu path was also removed. Please ignore keyboard events from interactive descendants and restore a keyboard/context-menu action path.

Valid and helpful. The event-path analysis was precise: Enter/Space from the nested More button reached the tree handler, which acted on the parent row and prevented the native button click. I addressed it by limiting tree keyboard handling to events whose target is the row itself, with a regression test covering descendant controls. A useful improvement would be to include the minimal expected keyboard test sequence (focus More -> press Enter/Space -> menu opens; tool-set enablement is unchanged), which would make the acceptance criteria immediately executable.

🤖 **[P2] This test is declared while another test is executing, so Mocha never runs it.** `reads marketplace plugin versions` needs to be a sibling under the suite, not nested inside `invalidates overlapping renders`. CI stays green because this assertion is never collected; move the closing brace so the version test is registered during suite definition.

AI Review: This availability callback can reactivate a stopped completion session. The listener exists before any request, and `trigger()` unconditionally sets `_isActive`, so an unmetered transition may fetch and show suggestions before the first user trigger or after Escape cleared the session. Please fire only `_providerAvailabilityChangeSignal` here; the existing active-session precondition will still refresh active work without reviving an inactive model. Coverage before the first request and after `stop()` would catch this.

Fixed in 8474b6eaab4. The availability listener now fires only `_providerAvailabilityChangeSignal`; it no longer calls `trigger()`, so it cannot set `_isActive`. The existing derived fetch precondition refreshes active sessions only. Coverage verifies transitions neither fetch before the first trigger nor reactivate after `stop()`.

The regression test starts the restore before switching sessions, so queueReconcile returns early and this _reconcile guard is never exercised. The path this guard is intended to protect—work queued immediately before a restore starts—could regress while the test remains green. Please add a case that queues reconciliation first, starts a gated restore before the sequencer callback runs, and verifies replacement waits for restore end.
